'''Christina Bohannan''' (born July 2, 1971)<ref name="Little Village Mage 2021-07-04">{{Cite news |url=https://littlevillagemag.com/christina-bohannan-party-iowa-democrats/|title=Iowa Democrats talk politics, hint at future campaigns at a party for Rep. Christina Bohannan |work=Little Village Magazine |date=4 July 2021}}</ref> is an American politician and law professor who served from 2021 to 2023 as the [[Iowa House of Representatives|Iowa state representative]] for the [[Iowa's 85th House of Representatives district|85th House district]]. A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], she was elected in [[2020 Iowa House of Representatives election|2020]], succeeding [[Vicki Lensing]].

Bohannan was the unsuccessful Democratic nominee for {{ushr|IA|1}} in [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa#District 1|2022]] and [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa#District 1|2024]], losing to [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Mariannette Miller-Meeks]]. She won the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa#District 1|2026 election]], defeating Miller-Meeks on her third try.

== Early life and education ==
Bohannan was born in 1971 and grew up in [[Florida]].<ref name="Little Village Mage 2021-07-04" /><ref name=":2" /> She was the youngest of three children.<ref name=":2" /> Her father was a construction worker, and her mother worked at a daycare.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Shillcock |first=George |date=August 24, 2021 |title=State Rep. Christina Bohannan of Iowa City announces bid to take on Mariannette Miller-Meeks |url=https://www.press-citizen.com/story/news/2021/08/24/state-rep-christina-bohannan-run-congress-iowas-2nd-district-challenge-mariannette-miller-meeks/8241970002/ |access-date=July 10, 2026 |website=Iowa City Press-Citizen |language=en-US}}</ref>

She earned a Bachelor of Science degree in [[environmental engineering]] from the [[University of Florida]] in [[Gainesville, Florida|Gainesville]] and a [[Juris Doctor]] from the University of Florida [[Fredric G. Levin College of Law|Levin College of Law]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Christina Bohannan |publisher=College of Law - The University of Iowa|url=https://law.uiowa.edu/people/christina-bohannan|access-date=2021-04-21 |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Bohannan began her career as an environmental engineer with the [[Florida Department of Environmental Protection]] in the 1990s.<ref name="jsteppe">{{cite news |last1=Steppe |first1=John |title=UI law professor Christina Bohannan defeats Rep. Lensing in Iowa House primary |url=https://www.thegazette.com/government-politics/ui-law-professor-christina-bohannan-defeats-rep-lensing-in-iowa-house-primary/ |access-date=August 12, 2021 |work=The Gazette |date=June 2, 2020}}</ref> She then attended law school and, after graduating, served as a [[law clerk]] for a federal judge on the [[United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Cook |first=Linda |last2=Niedelman |first2=Jim |date=August 14, 2022 |title=Christina Bohannan confident voters interested in individual more than Democrat or Republican |url=https://www.ourquadcities.com/news/4-the-record/christina-bohannan-confident-voters-interested-in-individual-more-than-democrat-or-republican/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929012024/https://www.ourquadcities.com/news/4-the-record/christina-bohannan-confident-voters-interested-in-individual-more-than-democrat-or-republican/ |archive-date=September 29, 2022 |access-date=July 10, 2026 |work=[[WHBF-TV]] (Channel 4; CBS affiliate) – OurQuadCities.com |publisher=[[Nexstar Media Group]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2000, she moved to Iowa, where she became a professor of law at the [[University of Iowa College of Law]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Brennan |first1=Paul |title='Democracy means voter choice': Christina Bohannan kicks off her campaign for the District 85 seat in the Iowa House |url=https://littlevillagemag.com/democracy-means-voter-choice-christina-bohannan-kicks-off-her-campaign-for-the-district-85-seat-in-the-iowa-house/ |access-date=August 12, 2021 |work=Little Village Magazine |date=November 14, 2019}}</ref> While teaching at the [[University of Iowa]] in [[Iowa City, Iowa|Iowa City]], Bohannan served as president of the faculty senate.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Harrell |first1=Kelsey |title=UI law professor launches bid for Iowa House |url=https://dailyiowan.com/2019/10/21/ui-law-professor-launches-bid-for-iowa-house/ |access-date=August 12, 2021 |work=Daily Iowan |date=October 21, 2019}}</ref>

== Iowa House of Representatives ==
Bohannan announced her candidacy for the [[Iowa House of Representatives, District 85|85th district]] seat in the [[Iowa House of Representatives]] in October 2019.<ref name="lvcampaignstart">{{cite news |last1=Brennan |first1=Paul |title=Christina Bohannan announces run for an Iowa City seat in the Iowa House of Representatives |url=https://littlevillagemag.com/christina-bohannan-announces-run-for-an-iowa-city-seat-in-the-iowa-house-of-representatives/ |access-date=August 12, 2021 |work=Little Village Magazine |date=October 21, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Zachary Oren |title=UI law professor Bohannan to primary Lensing for Iowa House District 85 |url=https://www.press-citizen.com/story/news/2019/10/21/ui-law-professor-bohannan-primary-lensing-iowa-house-district-85/4052652002/ |access-date=August 12, 2021 |work=Iowa City Press Citizen |date=October 21, 2019}}</ref> She defeated incumbent legislator [[Vicki Lensing]] by 32 percentage points in the Democratic primary<ref name="jsteppe" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=White |first1=Lauren |title=Christina Bohannan wins Democratic nomination for the Iowa House |url=https://dailyiowan.com/2020/06/02/christina-bohannan-wins-democratic-nomination-for-the-iowa-house-over-incumbent/ |access-date=August 12, 2021 |work=The Daily Iowan |date=June 2, 2020}}</ref> and won the general election unopposed.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Draisey |first1=Brooklyn |title=Johnson County keeps Democrats in uncontested seats |url=https://dailyiowan.com/2020/11/04/johnson-county-keeps-democrats-in-uncontested-seats/ |access-date=August 12, 2021 |work=The Daily Iowan |date=November 4, 2020}}</ref>

During her tenure, Bohannan helped advance [[Bipartisanship|bipartisan]] legislation addressing [[human trafficking]] and elder abuse, and opposed a proposed constitutional amendment declaring that the [[Iowa Constitution]] does not protect a right to abortion.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barton |first=Tom |date=August 24, 2021 |title=Iowa City Rep. Christina Bohannan announces run for Mariannette Miller-Meeks’ seat in Congress |url=https://www.thegazette.com/news/politics/iowa-city-rep-christina-bohannan-announces-run-for-mariannette-miller-meeks-seat-in-congress/article_25ea91ee-2bfd-5885-94ef-5bfc4d928363.html |access-date=July 9, 2026 |website=The Gazette |language=en}}</ref>

In the Iowa House, she served on the Natural Resources and Veterans Affairs committees and the Agriculture and Natural Resources Appropriations Subcommittee.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Representative Christina Bohannan |url=https://www.legis.iowa.gov/legislators/legislator?ga=89&personID=30661 |access-date=July 9, 2025 |website=The Iowa Legislature}}</ref> She previously served on the Information Technology, Judiciary, and State Government committees.<ref name=":0" />

== U.S. House of Representatives campaigns ==
Bohannan ran for the [[United States House of Representatives]] in [[Iowa's 1st congressional district]] in the [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa|2022 election]]. She was the Democratic nominee but lost in the general election to incumbent Republican [[Mariannette Miller-Meeks]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dunlap|first=Natalie|title=UI law professor Christina Bohannan announces bid for Congress|url=https://dailyiowan.com/2021/08/24/ui-law-professor-christina-bohannan-announces-bid-for-congress/|access-date=2021-08-25|website=The Daily Iowan}}</ref> In August 2023, Bohannan announced another campaign for the same seat in the [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa|2024 election]] but was unsuccessful after a close race with Miller-Meeks which was decided after a recount.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Neukam |first=Stephen |date=2024-01-05 |title=Democrat Running on Abortion in Iowa House Race Smashes Fundraising Records (Exclusive) |url=https://themessenger.com/politics/democrat-running-on-abortion-in-iowa-house-race-smashes-fundraising-records-exclusive |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240105002104/https://themessenger.com/politics/democrat-running-on-abortion-in-iowa-house-race-smashes-fundraising-records-exclusive |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 5, 2024 |access-date=2024-01-05 |website=The Messenger |language=en}}</ref> She announced a third run for the seat in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa|2026 election]] on June 17, 2025.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Altimari|first=Daniela|url=https://rollcall.com/2025/06/17/iowa-midterm-election-christina-bohannan/|title=Iowa Democrat launches third challenge to vulnerable GOP Rep. Miller-Meeks|work=[[Roll Call]]|date=June 17, 2025|access-date=June 17, 2025}}</ref> She won the Democratic primary in June 2026, advancing to the November general election.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Yilek |first1=Caitlin |title=Democrat Christina Bohannan to take on Iowa GOP Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks for third time in key swing district - CBS News |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/iowa-1st-congressional-district-democratic-primary-christina-bohannon-miller-meeks/ |access-date=17 June 2026 |publisher=CBS News |date=3 June 2026}}</ref>

== Political positions ==

=== Healthcare ===
Bohannan has advocated for [[Healthcare reform in the United States|healthcare reform]] aimed at expanding access to affordable health insurance. She supports making a public [[Medicare (United States)|Medicare]] buy-in available to Americans of any age and has called for extending enhanced subsidies under the [[Affordable Care Act]], reversing federal [[Medicaid]] cuts, and expanding Medicare to include dental, hearing, and vision benefits.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Payne |first=Marissa |date=January 27, 2026 |title=Democrat Christina Bohannan wants to allow Medicare buy-in at all ages |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/2026/01/27/democrat-christina-bohannan-wants-medicare-expansion-iowa-first-district/88359872007/ |access-date=July 9, 2026 |website=The Des Moines Register |language=en-US}}</ref> She has also supported allowing Medicare to negotiate lower prescription drug prices and extending the $35 monthly [[insulin]] cap to all Americans.<ref name=":1" />

=== Institutional reform ===
Bohannan has advocated for ethics reforms for Congress, including [[Term limits in the United States|term limits]] and age limits for members of Congress, banning congressional stock trading, and prohibiting members of Congress, their immediate families, and congressional staff from serving as [[Lobbying|lobbyists]].<ref name=":3" /> She has also supported establishing an independent bipartisan agency to investigate congressional ethics violations.<ref name=":3" />

== Personal life ==
Bohannan is married and has a daughter.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Henderson |first=O. Kay |date=2025-11-20 |title=First district candidate Bohannan backs age limits, ethics reforms for congress - Radio Iowa |url=https://www.radioiowa.com/2025/11/20/first-district-candidate-bohannan-backs-age-limits-ethics-reforms-for-congress/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260101194909/https://www.radioiowa.com/2025/11/20/first-district-candidate-bohannan-backs-age-limits-ethics-reforms-for-congress/ |archive-date=2026-01-01 |access-date=2026-07-10 |work=Radio Iowa |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hansen |first=Ryan |title=Bohannan criticizes Miller-Meeks as 'devastating and dangerous' abortion law takes effect |url=https://www.press-citizen.com/story/news/local/2024/07/29/bohannan-critical-of-miller-meeks-stance-on-new-6-week-abortion-ban/74587689007/ |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=Iowa City Press-Citizen |language=en-US|date=July 29, 2024}}</ref> She and her husband live in [[Iowa City, Iowa|Iowa City]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barton |first=Tom |date=2023-08-15 |title=Iowa City Democrat Christina Bohannan launches second U.S. House bid |url=https://www.thegazette.com/news/elections/iowa-city-democrat-christina-bohannan-launches-second-u-s-house-bid/article_070cfa94-05e7-5ce8-8e4f-3ac81ff10f4a.html |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=The Gazette |language=en}}</ref>
